Family or coach buys the device

SeeUsPlayPremium

SeeUsPlay, Inc. · Ashburn, Virginia, USA · founded 2022 · active · seeusplay.com · last verified 2026-09-19

Family or coach buys the devicePortable unitEvidence B€500 to €2,000 to start

SeeUsPlay is a dual-GoPro rig and app whose cloud AI turns two standard action cameras into an automatically tracked full-game video and highlight clips, paid for with tokens per game with no subscription seeusplay-01, seeusplay-02.

For Youth and amateur teams, mostly in the US, that want full-field automated recording delivered to YouTube at roughly $14 to $15 a game in 4K without a hardware lock-in or an annual fee seeusplay-01, seeusplay-03. It suits team managers who are happy to own GoPros, handle SD-card uploads and wait a few hours for processing seeusplay-04.

SeeUsPlay exists because standard GoPros already produce better raw video than most proprietary youth cameras, so the founders moved all the intelligence to the cloud and sold only a mount, a token and a processing job seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05. It matters now because token pricing with no off-season cost, full-game downloads on every plan and YouTube delivery attack the subscription model that funds Veo, Pixellot and Trace, and because the June 2026 move to 8K with the GoPro MISSION 1 shows a small vendor can ride the action-camera roadmap without building hardware seeusplay-02, seeusplay-06. It tells you that once capture is commodity hardware, the difference between vendors is the quality and price of the cloud production job and the terms attached to the footage seeusplay-03, seeusplay-07.

Price band Rig bundles $199 to $499 (sale prices, list $249 to $599) plus own GoPros; tokens $349 per 100 or $599 per 200 on sale, with a 4K game costing 4 tokens, 5K 5 tokens and 8K 10 tokens seeusplay-03

Italy The store lists US dollar prices with free shipping over $100 and no European reseller, retailer or Italian customer was found, while the terms state the service is hosted in the United States seeusplay-08, seeusplay-09.

The verdict

Look if You run a US youth or amateur team, you already own or are willing to buy two GoPros, and you want automated full-game video delivered to YouTube for about $14 a game with no annual commitment seeusplay-01, seeusplay-03. You should also look if resolution matters, since dual 5K and 8K capture from current GoPros exceeds every fixed youth camera seeusplay-02, seeusplay-06.

Skip if You need live streaming, since the workflow is record, upload from SD cards, process in the cloud and deliver hours later seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05. You should also skip it if you are in Europe or need a vendor with visible scale, since there is no European presence, the iOS app shows one rating, and the company discloses no funding, headcount or customer numbers seeusplay-08, seeusplay-09, seeusplay-10.

Watch-outs

  • There is no live streaming, and the vendor's own guidance is 15 minutes to a few hours of upload per 90-minute game followed by a processing turnaround of a few hours for 4K and 5K and up to eight hours for 8K seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06.
  • The terms grant SeeUsPlay an unrestricted, unlimited, irrevocable, perpetual, transferable, royalty-free licence over user contributions for promotional use and reserve the right to remove or disable files without notice seeusplay-09.
  • Token expiry rules are not published in the FAQ or the terms, so ask before buying a 200-token pack seeusplay-04, seeusplay-09.
  • The App Store seller is listed as SeeUssPlay LLC while the terms and Google Play name SeeUsPlay, Inc., and the Google Play listing shows 50+ downloads, so the customer base is small seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11.
  • The current headline prices are labelled Spring Sale in September 2026, so treat the $349 and $599 token prices as promotional and the $399 and $699 figures as list seeusplay-03.
  • Parents on a regional forum report no in-app preview and no recording indicator visible from behind the rig, and note the product lacks the event tagging and player tracking of Veo and Trace seeusplay-12.

Products

  • SeeUsPlay Rig (camera). Dual-GoPro mount and tripod system with battery packs for about 12 hours, compatible with HERO9 to HERO13 Black and MISSION 1 seeusplay-01, seeusplay-04.
  • SeeUsPlay app (iOS, Android) and web app (app). Controls both GoPros, manages teams and schedules, uploads footage, tracks token balances and delivers full games and highlights to YouTube or download seeusplay-06, seeusplay-10.
  • Follow AI cloud processing (platform). Cloud tracking and rendering from full-resolution footage with custom zoom levels, scoreboard overlay and sport-specific framing, paid per game with tokens seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06.

Profile against the 24 criteria

Use-case fit
SeeUsPlay covers soccer, American football including flag, rugby, baseball and softball, lacrosse, volleyball, basketball, field hockey and ice hockey, with soccer as the origin sport seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05, seeusplay-06. It fits teams that want a full-game record and highlights for review and family viewing after the match seeusplay-02. It does not fit clubs that need live distribution or a coaching analysis layer seeusplay-04, seeusplay-12.
Capture quality
Two GoPros on the rig capture 4K, 5K or 5.3K on HERO9 to HERO13 Black and up to 8K on the GoPro MISSION 1, and the cloud AI tracks from the raw full-resolution files seeusplay-01, seeusplay-02, seeusplay-04. Users can render several framing options per game, from no zoom to extra zoom, each as a separate video seeusplay-06. Parents describe the output as high quality with fairly reliable tracking seeusplay-12.
Automation accuracy
Tracking is performed in the cloud on full-resolution footage, which gives the model more pixels than on-device systems, and baseball received sport-specific dynamic framing in June 2026 seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06. Highlights are generated from events tagged by the user, there is no automatic event detection, and a parent notes the absence of auto tagging and player tracking compared with Veo and Trace seeusplay-02, seeusplay-12. No published accuracy figures exist.
Multi-angle and stitching
The system is built on two side-by-side GoPros whose footage the cloud combines into a single tracked full-field output seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05. Whether the output is a true stitched panorama or a virtual camera selecting between lenses is not documented. Not assessable further from public sources.
Latency and live readiness
There is no live streaming product, and delivery is measured in hours after the SD cards are uploaded seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05. The June 2026 update reduced turnaround to a few hours for 4K and 5K and eight hours or less for 8K, with same-day delivery expected for most games seeusplay-06.
Reliability and resilience
Reliability rests on GoPro hardware, with two battery packs giving about 12 hours of runtime for a tournament weekend, and a 30-day money-back guarantee on purchases seeusplay-01, seeusplay-07. Recording is local to the SD cards, so venue connectivity does not affect capture seeusplay-05. Parents mention the lack of a rear recording indicator as a practical failure risk seeusplay-12.
Portability and install
The rig is a dual-camera mount on a tripod, with bundles from Just the Basics at $199 to Everything You Need at $499 on sale seeusplay-01, seeusplay-03. Setup is described as snapping two GoPros on, raising the tripod and tapping record in the app seeusplay-05. GoPros are bought separately, and the HERO8 and earlier, the HERO11 Mini and the HERO (2024) are unsupported seeusplay-04.
Connectivity and bandwidth
Upload happens from the SD cards after the game through the mobile app or the web app, and the vendor's guidance is 15 minutes to a few hours per 90-minute game depending on camera bitrate and connection seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06. Dual 5K or 8K files are large, so a team without fast home or club broadband will feel the upload step seeusplay-04.
Workflow and UX
The three-step flow is record, create and share, with the app controlling both GoPros, the cloud building the full game and clips, and delivery direct to YouTube or download seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05. June 2026 brought a web app for team management, scheduling, token balances and uploads, a rebuilt mobile app with custom zoom, unified login and public documentation at docs.seeusplay.com seeusplay-06. Parents report no in-app preview before upload seeusplay-12.
Analysis layer
There is no analysis layer beyond user-tagged events that become highlights and an optional scoreboard overlay when scores are tagged seeusplay-02, seeusplay-05. Full-game downloads on every plan allow the file to go into any third-party analysis tool seeusplay-04.
Integrations
Delivery integrations are YouTube auto-upload to a team channel and Google Drive, both permitted only with the user's consent according to the privacy policy, plus direct download seeusplay-05, seeusplay-13. Sign-in supports Google, Facebook, Apple and email seeusplay-06. No league platform or analysis integrations are documented.
Distribution and OTT
Distribution is outsourced to YouTube, which keeps SeeUsPlay out of the paywall and subscription business and means families watch on a channel the team controls seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05. There is no viewer app, no pay-per-view and no live feed seeusplay-04.
Data access and ownership
Full game downloads are included on every plan with no paywall, so the team always holds a copy seeusplay-01, seeusplay-04. The terms grant SeeUsPlay an unrestricted, perpetual, transferable licence over user contributions for promotional use, place responsibility for transmitted data on the user and allow the company to remove or disable files without notice, and storage retention periods are not published seeusplay-09. Ownership of the underlying footage is not addressed in the FAQ seeusplay-04.
Privacy and compliance
The privacy policy, updated 16 June 2026, names SeeUsPlay, Inc., lists names, emails, club and team names and game information as collected data, states that the service does not knowingly market to children under 18 and requires parental consent for minors' accounts, and includes a section on legal bases that mirrors GDPR language seeusplay-13. The terms state the services are hosted in the United States and that international users consent to processing there seeusplay-09. The app store privacy labels list contact info and identifiers for analytics and functionality seeusplay-10. Facial recognition and biometrics are not mentioned seeusplay-13.
Security
Not assessable from public sources beyond the statements that YouTube and Google Drive access is used only for uploads and that the company keeps backups without liability for loss seeusplay-09, seeusplay-13.
Pricing and TCO
Tokens cost $349 per 100 or $599 per 200 on the current sale, against list prices of $399 and $699, and a game costs 4 tokens in 4K, 5 in 5K and 10 in 8K, so a 100-token pack covers 25 games in 4K, 20 in 5K or 10 in 8K seeusplay-03, seeusplay-04. Rig bundles are $199 and $499 on sale, list $249 and $599, and GoPros are extra seeusplay-03. A team filming 25 games a season in 4K therefore spends about $349 in tokens plus a one-off rig and two cameras, with zero cost in the off-season, which the vendor itself puts at about $15 a game and half the price of subscription rivals seeusplay-05, seeusplay-14. YouTube upload and full downloads carry no extra charge seeusplay-04.
Support and service
Support is by email at support@seeusplay.com and a web form, with published setup, user and application guides since June 2026 and a 30-day money-back guarantee seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06, seeusplay-07. No phone support, SLA or reseller network is published.
Company health and roadmap
SeeUsPlay, Inc. is a private company with its registered developer address in Ashburn, Virginia and Virginia governing law, and it discloses no funding, revenue, headcount or customer numbers seeusplay-09, seeusplay-11. The product cadence is active, with multi-sport support in July 2025, 8K, baseball, a web app and a rebuilt mobile app in June 2026, and iOS updates through September 2026 seeusplay-06, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-14. Google Play shows 50+ downloads and the US App Store one rating, which points to a small base seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11.
Evidence and references
Primary evidence is the SeeUsPlay site, FAQ, how-it-works page, update blog, terms and privacy policy, plus the Apple and Google store listings seeusplay-01, seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05, seeusplay-06, seeusplay-09, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11, seeusplay-13. Third-party evidence is one DC Urban Moms parent thread from March 2025 seeusplay-12. No press coverage, funding record or independent review was found.
Coach and analyst satisfaction
A parent with a season of use reports high-quality video, fairly reliable tracking and no buyer's regret, while noting the missing preview, the hidden recording indicator and the absence of auto tagging and player tracking seeusplay-12. Store ratings are too few to be meaningful seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11.
Edge versus cloud
SeeUsPlay is a pure cloud production model, with dumb capture on GoPros and all tracking, framing and rendering done after upload seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05. This gives it resolution headroom and lets it adopt new GoPro models quickly, at the cost of delivery latency and upload burden seeusplay-06.
Accessibility and languages
The apps are in English on iOS and Android, and the web app runs in a desktop browser seeusplay-06, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11. No other languages or European storefront pricing are published.
Upgrade path
Upgrades come from buying newer GoPros, since the same rig and tokens work across HERO9 to MISSION 1, and from choosing higher resolutions at more tokens per game seeusplay-02, seeusplay-04. There is no path into live streaming or analysis from the same vendor seeusplay-04.
Differentiators worth testing
Test the per-game token economics against your actual season length, since zero off-season cost is the core pitch seeusplay-03, seeusplay-05. Test the SD-card upload time from a typical club connection for a dual 5K game, since that is the workflow's weak point seeusplay-04. Test the 8K MISSION 1 output at extra zoom on a full-size pitch to see whether the resolution headroom translates into usable close framing seeusplay-06.

Company

Ownership and funding SeeUsPlay, Inc. is a private US company with its developer address at 22070 Auction Barn Dr, Ashburn, Virginia and Virginia governing law in its terms; the iOS seller is shown as SeeUssPlay LLC seeusplay-09, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11. No investors or funding rounds are disclosed.

Financials not public

Scale, company-stated Google Play shows 50+ downloads as of September 2026 and the US App Store shows one rating at 5.0 seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11. The company states soccer teams around the world have adopted the camera, without numbers seeusplay-14.
